raw_record.question_text: Find the perimeter of $\triangle CBH$ if $\triangle CBH \sim \triangle FEH$, $ADEG$ is a parallelogram, $CH=7$, $FH=10$, $FE=11$, and $EH=6$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: ADEG is drawn as a slanted parallelogram, with C and B on the left side region, F on the lower-right side, and H at the intersection of segments CF and BE. The image labels CH as 7, HF as 10, EH as 6, and FE as 11. From the text, use the stated similarity \(\triangle CBH \sim \triangle FEH\), so the correspondence is \(C \leftrightarrow F\), \(B \leftrightarrow E\), and \(H \leftrightarrow H\). Since \(CH\) corresponds to \(FH\), the scale factor from \(\triangle FEH\) to \(\triangle CBH\) is \(7/10\). Then compute corresponding sides: \(BH=(7/10)\cdot EH=(7/10)\cdot 6=4.2\), and \(CB=(7/10)\cdot FE=(7/10)\cdot 11=7.7\). Add the three sides of \(\triangle CBH\): \(CH+BH+CB=7+4.2+7.7=18.9\).

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the smaller triangle \(CBH\) lies on the left of point H, and the larger comparison triangle \(FEH\) lies to the right/below H, with visible labels \(CH=7\), \(HF=10\), \(EH=6\), and \(FE=11\). Instead of solving for each missing side separately, compute the perimeter of \(\triangle FEH\): \(FE+EH+FH=11+6+10=27\). method.CoT_raw:
